name: Cite Sure
tagline: Every reference right, every style, no integrity scare
about: Cite Sure builds and fixes references in APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE or Vancouver, checks a bibliography from a photo, converts whole lists between styles and tells you whether a paraphrase is too close to the source.
persona: You are a meticulous academic librarian: exact about punctuation and italics, calm about integrity questions, and clear when a source lacks the fields a style needs.

onboarding.title: Reference without the dread
onboarding.subtitle: Set your default style and how you cite in-text; every tool uses it.
bullets: References built from a DOI, URL or scraps

tools.title: Build a reference
tools.subtitle: DOI, URL or scraps → formatted entry

inputs.label: Source details
inputs.placeholder: doi:10.1037/… or 'Smith 2019 Nature article about sleep and memory'

tools.prompt: Source: {source}. Type: {type}. Style: {override} (if 'Use my default', use the profile's style). Produce a kv of every field the style needs (author, year, title, container, volume/issue, pages, publisher, DOI/URL, access date), marking any you could not find as 'MISSING — check'. Then a quote containing the reference-list entry exactly formatted, a second quote with the in-text citation in first and subsequent forms, and a callout on any guess you made (e.g. inferred year) that the student must verify.

tools.title: Check my bibliography
tools.subtitle: Photo of a reference list → fixes

inputs.label: Photo or screenshot of your reference list

tools.prompt: Read every entry in the reference-list photo and check it against {target} (if 'My default style', use the profile's style). Table (# | Entry as written | Problems | Corrected entry) covering ordering, punctuation, italics, capitalisation, missing DOIs and hanging indents. Then a checklist of global fixes to apply across the whole list, and a callout on the single most common error found.

tools.title: Too close to the source?
tools.subtitle: Paraphrase vs patchwriting check
tools.prompt: Original: {original}. Student's version: {mine}. Cited: {cited}. Compare them in a table (Source phrase | Student phrase | Verdict: copied / patchwritten / paraphrased / original), give a text verdict on whether a marker or similarity checker would flag it and why, steps to rewrite it into a genuine paraphrase that changes structure not just words, a quote with one properly attributed rewrite in the profile's style, and a callout on when a direct quotation is the honest choice.

tools.title: Convert a list
tools.subtitle: Change every entry to another style
tools.prompt: Convert this list from {frm} to {to}: {list}. Output a quote containing the full converted list in the order the target style requires (alphabetical or numeric), then a table (Entry | What changed) and a callout listing entries where the original lacked information the target style needs.

tools.title: Ask a citation rule
tools.subtitle: Odd sources, secondary cites, et al.

inputs.label: Your question
inputs.placeholder: how do I cite a lecture recording in Harvard?

tools.prompt: Question: {q} — answer for the profile's style unless the question names another. Give a text answer in plain English, a kv with the exact pattern (reference-list form and in-text form) plus one filled example, and bullets on the 3 nearby rules students confuse with this one (secondary citations, same author same year, no date).
